title: Why S-Traps Fail in DWV Systems
description: S-traps were once common in residential installations, but modern plumbing codes prohibit them because they frequently self-siphon. When water rushes down a vertical drop immediately following the trap, momentum and pressure differentials create a siphon that pulls the water seal straight out of the trap basin. Without this vital water seal, noxious sewer gases freely enter the living space. Correcting an illegal S-trap requires installing a vented P-trap configuration or using an Air Admittance Valve (AAV) where permitted by local jurisdiction, maintaining atmospheric pressure balance and preserving the trap seal.

Without this vital water seal, noxious sewer gases freely enter the living space. Correcting an illegal S-trap requires installing a vented P-trap configuration or using an Air Admittance Valve (AAV) where permitted by local jurisdiction, maintaining atmospheric pressure balance and preserving the trap seal.
